newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas steady to lower amid weak demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas steady to lower amid weak demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were steady to lower Wednesday amid moderate weather patterns across most of the U.S. and a wavering futures market, industry sources said.
Prices at the Henry Hub, La, on average were down one cent from Tuesday to $2.20-2.21 per mmBtu, while Transco (Station 65) was quoted mostly in the low-to-mid $2.20s.
NYMEX's June Henry Hub gas futures bounced back and forth between $2.16 and $2.22 in Wednesday's session following Tuesday's settlement at $2.191.
Buyers continued to pump gas into storage, which prevented prices from stretching their losses, market sources said.

Also lending some support to the market was the ongoing maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which will continue to cut about 400 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) out of a total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Thursday.

Also, Mobil Corp said maintenance at its Mary Ann gas plant in Coden, Ala., is expected to last until mid-June. Total capacity of the plant is 380-390 mmcfd, and about 120 mmcfd is due back within a week.
South Texas prices also slipped one cent to $2.10-2.11, while west Texas prices in the Permian basin were flat to one cent lower at $1.96-2.00.
At the southern California border, turned-back supplies from the West Coast pressured prices to about $2.14-2.16, traders said.
In the East, New York city-gate prices remained in the mid-$2.40s, while Appalachian prices fell an average of two cents to about $2.37-2.40.
In the Midcontinent, where temperatures are expected to remain below normal through early next week, prices were steady to one cent lower at $2.01-2.02.
Chicago city-gate was quoted in the low-$2.20s, while Detroit city-gate prices were around $2.33.
